deep_dive.title: Combinatorial perturbation structure enables graded inference of signaling activity by CIRCE
deep_dive.abstract: Cells decode external inputs into intracellular activities of varying magnitude, and inferring both input identity and strength is crucial for cell-fate engineering. However, perturbation-response models typically treat all cells exposed to a given input as a discrete class, ignoring cell-to-cell variation in response magnitude. Here, we introduce a structured-label framework that infers both input identity and strength from combinatorial perturbation screens without dose-resolved training labels. We represent each perturbation combination in a binary combinatorial space and replace one-hot supervision with a Boltzmann distribution that decays with the Hamming distance between combinations. This approach preserves classification accuracy while improving calibration and resolving continuous pathway activities across individual cells. Importantly, intermediate scores primarily reflect ambiguity in cellular response states rather than insufficient model knowledge. Applied to engineered and natural tissues, the calibrated model successfully recovered graded activities. These results establish combinatorial perturbation screens as a self-calibrating framework for decoding graded cellular responses.

deep_dive.title: Mapping whole-tissue spatial multi-omics at single-cell resolution with STEP
deep_dive.abstract: Spatial omics technologies have revolutionized our ability to map transcriptomic, proteomic, or metabolomic profiles within tissue contexts. However, existing spatial multi-omics approaches emphasize clustering or domain identification from measured profiles, while a general framework for whole-slice mapping in measured and unmeasured areas at single-cell resolution across additional omics layers remains lacking. Here we introduce STEP, a computational framework that integrates probabilistic inference with deep learning for flexible integration of histology, spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT), single-cell, and/or multi-omics data. We validated STEP's advantages across diverse applications. Furthermore, STEP enables tri-modal integration of Xenium, CITE-seq, and imaging mass cytometry to map transcriptome-wide gene expression and protein profiles from a small gene panel. Through quadra-modal integration of SRT, histology, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and inCITE-seq, STEP reconstructs a 3D multi-omics brain cell atlas from six low-resolution SRT sections. Collectively, STEP provides a cost-effective tool for exploring spatial biology by integrating diverse, complementary modalities.

quick_skim.title: An Explainable and Scalable Hierarchical Tensor Framework for Integrating Multi-Omics and Digital Pathomics
quick_skim.abstract: Background: Precision oncology requires integration of heterogeneous molecular and pathology data, yet many fusion models offer limited biologically grounded interpretability and struggle with missing modalities.   Methods: We present Hierarchical Interpretable Tensor Fusion (HIT-Fuse), integrating six modalities: somatic copy number variation, DNA methylation, RNA sequencing, microRNA expression, RPPA protein abundance, and vision transformer-derived pathomics across four TCGA cohorts (glioma, lung adenocarcinoma, breast, and kidney cancer). Modality-specific autoencoders compress high-dimensional inputs, followed by two-stage CP tensor decomposition. Missing latent modalities are reconstructed using clinical covariates and observed omics to expand cohorts and retrain downstream models. A mathematical traceback mechanism enables global and local xAI attributions.   Results: HIT-Fuse identifies distinct latent subgroups with significant survival stratification in glioma, breast, and kidney cohorts, both with complete and reconstructed modalities. Cohort expansion yields cohort-specific gains, including a 56.4% relative increase in weighted F1 for glioma. Biological validation against DepMap CRISPR screens, miRTarBase and RPPA annotations supports decoded drivers across all four cohorts. Essential gene rates range from 6.2% in glioma to 7.6% in lung cancer; example drivers include ANAPC11, SNRPD1, PLK1 and RPL14. Of decoded miRNAs, 71-92% have miRTarBase regulatory support, while 77-84% of selected genes are covered in DepMap.   Conclusions: HIT-Fuse combines hierarchical tensor fusion, missing-modality reconstruction and traceable attributions to support interpretable multi-omics and digital pathology-based cancer prognosis across heterogeneous cohorts.

quick_skim.title: LIFT: Latent Flow Matching for Probabilistic Cell Fate Dynamics with Single Cell Snapshots
quick_skim.abstract: Lineage tracing links cell states through clonal ancestry, but does not generally identify unique source-descendant pairings. Learning from such data therefore requires a model of conditional outcomes, rather than only the terminal population distribution. We introduce LIFT, a latent flow framework for probabilistic cell-state generation from lineage-informed couplings. Variational inference encodes alternative outcomes in a latent space, while a conditional prior enables sampling from the initial state alone. A Mean Flow decoder predicts future cell state directly, requiring one decoder evaluation per sampling, which makes it convenient to predict cell fate through large scale Monte-Carlo sampling. This construction combines a representation of one-to-many relationships with efficient sampling and an analysis of conditional prediction error. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate LIFT's ability to recover both population distribution and cell fate probabilities.
